customization.summary: Managed CPU-only Firecracker sandbox with custom image-derived templates and CPU/RAM sizing at template build time, network rules, pause/resume and private-beta volumes. Inspected integration uses e2b_code_interpreter.Sandbox.create(timeout=180) with no explicit template or resource sizing. Official default RAM descriptions conflict; tested allocation is unknown. BYOC is E2B-operated and distinct from self-hosted Embed.

features.notes: Managed templates can derive from Docker registry images, existing templates or parsed Dockerfiles. Distribution/package requirements apply; scratch/distroless and multistage Dockerfile conversion are unsupported. Adapter does not select/build a custom template, and the Code Interpreter SDK default must not be confused with generic Sandbox base.

Existing dependency_install evaluations pass installation/import of an uploaded offline wheel in a private directory using --no-index/--no-deps. This tests runtime Python package installation, not internet package registry connectivity or apt/sudo privileges.

cpu_count/cpuCount is configured in Template.build, not a cpu keyword in this adapter's create call. Pricing lists 1-8 vCPUs; billing docs list 8 Hobby, 8+ Pro by support request, custom Enterprise. Adapter does not request CPU and reports do not inventory allocation.

memory_mb/memoryMB at template build; pricing bills GiB-seconds and lists 1-8 GiB, with support-approved higher Pro/Enterprise limits in billing docs. Pricing says default 4 GiB, generic base-image docs say 512 MiB, and billing FAQ repeats 512 MiB. Do not infer default Code Interpreter or tested RAM from these descriptions; adapter leaves sizing unset.

Official GPU FAQ explicitly states sandboxes are CPU-only with no GPU SDK/CLI/API/template option; BYOC does not change this. Calling remote inference, installing CUDA libraries, or running an agent that orchestrates GPU training elsewhere is not local sandbox GPU access.

Default public egress; allow_internet_access switch, IP/CIDR allow/deny rules, HTTP 80 Host and TLS 443 SNI domain allowlisting. Allow rules override denies; domain mode requires deny-all and allows default DNS server. Domain filtering does not cover QUIC/other ports and shared endpoints have limitations. Runtime update_network replaces rules. Adapter uses defaults and tests no custom policy.

Pause/resume preserves filesystem and memory; paused retention is indefinite until explicit kill. Persistent volumes independent of sandbox lifetime are in private beta with locking/ownership limitations. Adapter kills at cleanup and mounts no volume; measured session state is not persistence after kill.

Connect to a running/paused sandbox; adapter retains one Code Interpreter sandbox across calls and session_state evaluation passes three separate filesystem calls. The fixture does not prove Python-variable continuity or pause/resume. Continuous runtime caps are 1h Hobby/24h Pro, reset after pause/resume; adapter timeout is 180s.

Provider commands.run supports foreground/background shell commands. Adapter instead submits all code to run_code with no language selector, so generic shell capability is not a native shell-request route in this integration.

files.write/read APIs; adapter transfers input bytes, reads output with format=bytes and hashes it. Existing artifact_roundtrip validates 26900 bytes; offline-wheel install also exercises binary input staging. One-level output listing does not establish recursive directory or maximum-size transfer support.

get_host(port) generates a public HTTPS proxy URL for sandbox services, with optional public-access restrictions. URLs are public by default; proxy terminates TLS and can re-encrypt to configured HTTPS ports, not TLS passthrough. Adapter configures no service/preview or public-access restriction.

Official open-source runtime/control plane is Apache-2.0. BYOC docs distinguish self-operated single-machine Embed on Linux/KVM from E2B-operated Enterprise clusters in customer AWS/GCP/Azure accounts. This adapter and its evaluations use managed Code Interpreter; no self-hosted parity or deployment was tested.

No provider-native customer KMS key binding/rotation/revocation contract was verified in inspected pricing, API-facing and BYOC documentation. Customer-account storage locality in BYOC does not itself establish CMEK coverage for all sandbox data. Adapter declares false but does not test key management.

pricing.model: Monthly plan fee plus provisioned vCPU/RAM per running sandbox-second; paused/killed compute not billed; included sandbox storage.

rates.unit: included plan allocation, no extra charge
month, minimum not a unit compute rate

pricing.limitations: Exact public rates retrieved 2026-10-13; no invoice or historical price comparison verified. Hobby has one-time $100 credits, 20 concurrency/1h continuous runtime/10 GiB storage; Pro 100 concurrency/24h/20 GiB storage and no additional credits. Pricing default is 2 vCPU/4 GiB while generic base/billing FAQ say 2 vCPU/512 MiB; Code Interpreter allocation and tier are unverified. 'Storage free' is scoped to included sandbox storage, not an independently priced beta-volume contract. Report fixed $0.00004/sec is estimate_unverified_rates and client wall time is not metered runtime.
